slides.title: Pinning third-party files by hash
slides.summary: SRI lets the browser refuse a script or stylesheet whose contents don't match the hash you expected.
body: When you load a script from a CDN, you trust whoever controls that CDN. If it's compromised, every site using it runs the attacker's code.
Subresource Integrity adds an integrity attribute with a cryptographic hash of the file. The browser downloads it, hashes it, and refuses to run it if the hash doesn't match.

ul: Add crossorigin="anonymous", so the browser can read a cross-origin response to check it.
Pin exact versions in the URL. A floating @latest URL changes, and the hash then blocks it.

body: <mark>SRI only works for files that never change. It suits versioned library builds, not analytics tags that update themselves.</mark>
code: curl -s URL | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A

steps.caption: The browser fetches the file as usual.
